question:
FRONT-PAGE WORDING, from the owner of PaperTrades.AI (Sat Oct 31, 2 p.m. ET). NOT a trading turn. The owner: "Is this not misleading to have on the front page when it's fake money? Maybe we can say best judgement or something. Check with the other AIs; if they think it's fine, stay with it; but check legally." Majority wins.

THE FRONT PAGE NOW (the first thing a visitor reads):
  Headline: "Which AI makes the most money?"
  Line under it: "Claude vs Gemini vs ChatGPT · C$100,000 of pretend money each · 10 races, from stocks to sports bets · real prices · Oct 28 to Nov 28. Every trade and every reason is public."
  Then: "Right now: 👑 Gemini leads overall (+C$15,659 total profit)."

CONTEXT: The site is run from British Columbia, Canada; most visitors are Canadian, some US. Nothing is sold; no real money is invested or bet; the site gives no advice, and every page says simulation only. Canada's Competition Act judges a claim by its "general impression" on an ordinary reader, not only its literal words; Canadian securities regulators watch online content that looks like investment advice or performance promotion; sports-bet content is sensitive for advertising (the site takes no bets and links to no sportsbook).

OPTIONS (vote for ONE or AMEND, with the main reason and any risk):
H1. Keep it as is (the sub-line already says pretend money).
H2. "Which AI makes the most (pretend) money?" plus the same sub-line.
H3. "Which AI has the best judgment with money?" plus the sub-line, and the leader line reads "Right now: 👑 Gemini leads overall (+C$15,659 in pretend money)".
H4. "Which AI makes the best money calls?" with "Pretend money, real prices" in the sub-line's first words.
H5. Your own wording (headline at most 8 words).
Also: is "+C$15,659 total profit" on the front page misleading without "pretend"? One line.

Answer as: Vote: ... / Reason: ... / Risk: ... / Leader line: ...

chatgpt.answer:
Vote: H2, amended so the leader line also says pretend money.

Reason: It preserves the clear hook, but puts “pretend” in the headline itself, which is safer for the ordinary-reader/general-impression test. “Best judgment” or “best money calls” could sound more like investment advice or performance promotion.

Risk: Still slightly promotional because it ranks AIs by “money” and uses C$ figures, so the simulation language should appear before or beside every profit/leader figure.

Leader line: Yes — “+C$15,659 total profit” is potentially misleading without “pretend”; use: “Right now: 👑 Gemini leads overall (+C$15,659 in pretend-money profit).”

gemini.answer:
Vote: H2, with the leader line amended to include "pretend money".

Reason: Under Canada's Competition Act, the "general impression" of the primary headline must not be deceptive; adding "(pretend)" directly into the headline instantly neutralizes regulatory risk while keeping the clear, objective metric (money) rather than a subjective one (judgment), and avoids the word "calls" which securities regulators might interpret as unregistered investment advice.

Risk: Using parentheses slightly disrupts the visual punch and flow of the main headline, but this is a minor trade-off for absolute regulatory safety. 

Leader line: Yes, stating "+C$15,659 total profit" without a qualifier could give a skimming reader the general impression of real financial returns, so it must be amended to "pretend money" or "paper profit".
